overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the December 8 notice was sufficiently specific, and the remaining allegations were declined as outside the OML or too unspecific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the December 8 meeting notice was not specific enough because it omitted a bylaw violation the complainant was said to have committed.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a meeting notice to list all tangential issues related to a particular topic.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board let individuals make defaming remarks against the complainant during the meeting, citing G.L. c. 87.
allegations.key_passage: We have previously declined to review complaints alleging that a public body has violated c. 87, or that a public body subjected a complainant to hostile treatment.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the conduct of the meeting violated G.L. c. 87, the shade tree statute.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to impartially hear the complainant's tree removal appeal, a G.L. c. 87 matter.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, we decline to review such allegations here.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board gave insufficient individual notice of the meeting to the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require additional notice of an open session meeting beyond the meeting notice itself.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair deliberated with a quorum of the Board outside a meeting, but cited no specific communication.
allegations.key_passage: However, the complaint does not cite to any improper communication outside a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
